clue.text: Related to a clergy member's completed exam

parts.note: something completed is over and done, in the past
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A clergy member's exam, now finished, is the subject of some related talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral care is the work of a minister or priest looking after a flock, so the word describes clerical duties.

clue.text: See 15
Undaunted, I say 'Fancy Cher coming round!'

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come round, enclosing the exclamation
fancy as a verb hints at a fanciful rearrangement of the letters of the singer's name

parts.note: 'I say!' and 'Oi!' are both calls to get attention

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly praises the singer Cher for paying a visit, adding that she is fearless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' rearranges the singer's name to HERC, and 'coming round' wraps it about the exclamation, which matches 'I say!' as a cry for attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undaunted shows courage in the face of danger, like a hero.

clue.text: Every sort of grey sensitivity

parts.note: every one means all of them

indicators.note: a sort of grey is a variant of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Every shade of grey has its own delicacy, as if colours had feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges GREY into ERGY.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergy is a bodily hypersensitivity to some substance such as pollen.

clue.text: Lambert occupies swell place to sleep in USA

indicators.note: one piece occupies the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: a swell is a fashionable dandy, a fop
L is the symbol for the lambert, a unit of luminance

explanation.surface: Someone called Lambert moves into a smart American guesthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like an adjective but is the old noun for a dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang a flop, short for flophouse, is a cheap lodging where one beds down for the night.

clue.text: Lacking a posh girl's traditional education? It's not done!

definitions.text: Lacking a posh girl's traditional education
definitions.meaning: wealthy girls were once sent to finishing school to learn etiquette, so one who missed it has not been finished

explanation.surface: A girl who skipped her social polishing is told sternly that it is simply not done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's not done!' looks like a remark on etiquette, matching the first half, but it is a plain second meaning: incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: A finishing school completed a young lady's training; without it she is, punningly, incomplete, as is any job left half-way.

clue.text: Beat trio, almost quiet

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a trio is three
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A band of three is told their beat is nearly quiet enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims THREE to THRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To thresh grain is to beat it to separate the seed; it also means to thrash or flail generally.

clue.text: Board attached to spring is so long

parts.note: board as in board and lodging is food, or fare
a spring is a source of water, a well

explanation.surface: A plank fixed to a coil turns out to be extremely lengthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a measure of the board but is the casual goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is an informal way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Meal project one's lacking

indicators.note: the larger word lacks this part, so it is removed

parts.note: to launch a scheme is to project or start it
a means one

explanation.surface: A catering project has only one thing missing: the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunch is the midday meal.

clue.text: See 26
Rather excessive pre-divorce settlement

indicators.note: a settlement arranges matters, so the letters are settled into a new order

explanation.surface: A divorce settlement agreed in advance looks rather steep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' looks like part of the legal picture but is the anagram signal for PREDIVORCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overpriced costs more than it is worth, an excessive charge.

clue.text: Temperature over Havana is dire

indicators.note: over signals the cigar word turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a Havana is a Cuban cigar

explanation.surface: A weather report says the heat over the Cuban capital is terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Havana' looks like the city but is a cigar; 'over' reverses it to RAGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A dire or calamitous event is tragic.

clue.text: It currently makes western Scotland more temperate

definitions.text: It currently makes western Scotland more temperate

parts.words: It currently makes western Scotland more temperate
parts.note: currently puns on an ocean current, the warm Atlantic flow that keeps the west of Scotland milder than its latitude suggests

explanation.definitionFit: This warm Atlantic current carries tropical water north-east and is credited with the mild climate of western Britain.

clue.text: Talk on fair's source of illumination

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
fair hair or skin is light

explanation.surface: A chat about a funfair throws light on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like a funfair but is the adjective meaning pale.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas lamp was a common source of street and household lighting before electricity.

clue.text: Tabloid support for south-east Asian inhabitant

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
to bear a weight is to support it

explanation.surface: A popular newspaper campaigns on behalf of someone living in South-East Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a well-known British tabloid newspaper. The 'inhabitant' is an animal, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun bear is a small bear native to the tropical forests of South-East Asia.

clue.text: Taking lead from a South African (deceased), act like Tarzan

indicators.note: taking away the lead, the first letter, of the word

parts.note: a Zulu is a member of a South African people
the late person is one who has died

explanation.surface: A dead South African's example inspires someone to swing through the jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking lead from' sounds like following an example but means dropping the first letter. The Zulus are a people of South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan's famous jungle call is a long wavering howl, which is what to ululate means.

clue.text: Play the politician, ousting queen

indicators.note: ousting means throwing out, so the queen's letter is removed

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
R is the abbreviation for regina, queen

explanation.surface: Someone plays the part of a politician who overthrows the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to play or trifle with it.

clue.text: Prince and circle not present in penthouse rave

indicators.note: these pieces are absent from the longer word, so they are taken out

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A prince and his social circle skip the party at the penthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rave' looks like the party but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rave about something is to enthuse, speaking of it with great excitement.

clue.text: Drink noisily, tossing off a litre — get up, then stagger

indicators.note: tossing off means discarding, so the letter is removed

parts.note: to slurp is to drink noisily
L is the abbreviation for a litre
to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: Someone gulps a drink, knocks back a litre, stands up and then reels about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stagger' looks like the drinker's walk but means to astonish.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish or amaze them.

clue.text: Gad about, like pirates at sea?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A question whether roaming around is what pirates do on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to wander about aimlessly or wearily, much as to gad about.

clue.text: One who refuses to snicker out loud at speaker

indicators.note: out loud means the word is heard spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: a horse's snicker is a whinny or neigh
a sayer is one who says things, a speaker

explanation.surface: A person who refuses snickers loudly at someone speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snicker' looks like a stifled laugh but is a horse's whinny.
explanation.definitionFit: A naysayer habitually refuses, denies or opposes things.

clue.text: Almost all wood furniture is from the mountains

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: pine is a wood much used for furniture, and pine furniture is a style

explanation.surface: Nearly all the timber furniture comes from the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine means belonging to high mountains, originally the Alps.

clue.text: Style for service gets go-ahead

parts.note: a mode is a manner or style
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A fashionable form of church service is given approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go-ahead' looks like permission but is the adjective meaning progressive.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-ahead outlook is progressive and up-to-date.

clue.text: Bullets etc found in moorhen's wings — God!

indicators.note: one piece is found inside the other
the wings of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: ammo is ammunition, bullets and the like

explanation.surface: Someone finds ammunition in a water bird's wings and exclaims in shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'God!' looks like an exclamation but is the definition. 'wings' gives M and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammon is the false god of riches, named in the Gospels.

clue.text: Shame about pump or biro

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is embarrassed over a pump and a ballpoint pen.
explanation.walkthrough: A biro is a British word for a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Opprobrium is public disgrace or harsh criticism.

clue.text: Mountain peak cracked by ace climber?

indicators.note: the outer word is cracked open and the other piece goes in

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain peak
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A star mountaineer breaks a mountain summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber?' looks like the mountaineer but is a climbing plant; the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: Runner and other beans are climbing plants, trained up poles.

clue.text: Secretive celebrity's large body not evident to viewers

definitions.text: large body not evident to viewers

parts.note: dark as in keep it dark means secret
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A shy celebrity has a big body that nobody gets to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers use the term for a massive object, such as a collapsed sun, that gives off no visible light.

clue.text: Does ancient history start after a point?

indicators.note: after places the first piece after the second

parts.note: a dot is a point

indicators.note: the start of the word means its first letter

explanation.surface: A question whether ancient history begins after a full stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ancient' looks like it belongs with history but goes with the definition: an old form of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the archaic third-person singular of do, used in the Bible and Shakespeare.

clue.text: Big city, one on western half of Salt Lake

parts.note: NY is New York, the Big Apple
a means one

indicators.note: the western half of an across word is its first half

explanation.surface: A big city sits on the west side of a salt lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Nyasa, now Lake Malawi, is one of the great lakes of East Africa.

clue.text: Like William Wallace's outdated tax, this is complicated

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free

indicators.note: complicated letters are tangled up, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old tax from Wallace's day is called tangled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is complicated' rearranges THIS into TISH. William Wallace was a medieval Scottish independence leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallace led the Scots against England, so his nationality is that of Scotland.
